title: 1 · Sounds, spelling and stress
blurb: Read Italian words aloud: pure vowels, soft and hard c and g, double consonants and stress.

title: 2 · Greetings: tu and Lei
blurb: Greet people at any time of day, say your name, and choose between tu and Lei.

title: 3 · Gender and number of nouns
blurb: Tell masculine from feminine nouns, learn the common exceptions, and make nouns plural.

title: 4 · Articles: il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le
blurb: Pick the right word for the and a by gender, number and the first sound of the noun.

title: 5 · Subject pronouns: io, tu, Lei, voi
blurb: Know the words for I, you, he, she, we and they, when to use Lei and voi, and when to leave them out.

title: 6 · essere and avere: I am, I have
blurb: Say who you are, where you're from, how old you are and how you feel, with essere and avere.

title: 7 · Adjectives: agreement and position
blurb: Describe clothes and people with adjectives that come after the noun and agree with it.

title: 8 · Present tense: -are, -ere, -ire
blurb: Conjugate regular verbs for every subject, including Lei and voi, and talk about work and study.

title: 9 · Questions and question words
blurb: Ask yes / no questions without any extra word, and use the question words for who, what, where, when, why, how and how many.

title: 10 · c'è and ci sono: there is, there are
blurb: Say what there is in town with c'è and ci sono, ask whether there is a pharmacy nearby, and tell c'è from è.

title: 11 · Numbers, time and dates
blurb: Count to a thousand, tell the time, give a date and ask what something costs in euros.

title: 12 · Possessives and demonstratives
blurb: Talk about your family and your things with my, your, his and her, and point at people with this and that.

title: 13 · Prepositions: a, di, da, in, and al, del, nel
blurb: Say where you live, where you are going and how, whose things they are, and join a, di, da, in and su with the article.

title: 14 · andare, fare, venire, stare
blurb: Use andare, venire, fare and stare in every person to say where you go, where you come from, what the weather is like and how you feel.

title: 15 · potere, dovere, volere
blurb: Say what you can, must and want to do, ask a stranger for help, and ask politely with vorrei.

title: 16 · piacere: mi piace, mi piacciono
blurb: Say what you and others like and don't like with mi piace and mi piacciono, and answer me too and me neither.

title: 17 · Reflexive verbs and daily routine
blurb: Describe your day, from waking up to getting dressed, and say what you and others are called.

title: 18 · Object pronouns: lo, la, li, le
blurb: Say "it", "them", "him" and "her" without repeating the noun: Lo prendo, Posso provarla?

title: 19 · Imperative and vorrei: ordering and asking
blurb: Order politely with vorrei, tell a friend what to do (or not to do), and understand what staff and strangers tell you.

title: 20 · Passato prossimo with avere
blurb: Say what you did yesterday, last week or two years ago: ho mangiato, hai visto, abbiamo fatto.

title: 21 · Passato prossimo with essere: sono andato, sono andata
blurb: Tell a trip story with sono andato, siamo arrivati and mi sono alzata, making the past participle agree.

title: 22 · Adverbs: time, place and quantity
blurb: Say how often, where and how much: sempre, non… mai, già, qui, lì, molto and troppo.

title: 23 · e, ma, perché, quando, se
blurb: Join your sentences with and, but, because, when, if and so, and say "me too" and "me neither".

title: 24 · sapere and conoscere: two ways to know
blurb: Choose the right "know" for facts, skills, people and places, and avoid the false friends that trip up English speakers.
